purpose: Show a founder exactly what working with Alliance AI Partners is like, step by step, so the process feels safe and they start an AI check-up.

seo.title: How we work | Alliance AI Partners
seo.description: Four steps: we learn how your business works, pick the right fix, build it, then keep it running and help you grow. Weekly updates, a person reviews every piece of work, and your data stays in your systems.

One continuous wide satin ribbon, in a gradient from Alliance Blue to Ribbon Cyan, runs across all four hills like a path, catching the light on each crest, and carries on out of frame at the upper right: four steps that keep going. A young faceted paper sapling stands on the last and highest hill. Soft slate-blue shadows, Partner Navy only in the deepest facets, a pale Daylight sky with calm empty space in the upper left quarter. Aspect about 1.08:1, safe to crop to 4:5. sections.name: Four steps
sections.job: Show the whole path once, on the ribbon, before each step is told in depth.
sections.desktop: Asymmetric head (title 0.9fr, lead 1.1fr), 48 px, Steps component (Desktop) full container width.

content.heading: Four steps from first call to growth.
content.lead: Every partnership follows the same path, and the last step doesn’t end at launch. Here is what happens at each one, what you get and what we need from you.

sections.name: Step 1 · Understand
sections.job: Explain that we listen first, what we ask, and that this is usually the AI check-up.
sections.desktop: Image 560x700 left, text column right (680). Title, mono meta below it, lead, 'What we ask' rows with mono numbers and hairlines, You get / From you rows, link.
sections.mobile: Title, meta, lead, image 4:5 under the lead, question rows, You get / From you, link.

content.heading: First, we listen.
content.lead: We learn how your business works and where it gets stuck. On the first call, we spend the first half asking questions, then repeat the problem back in your words before we suggest anything.

items.title: Walk us through what happens when a new customer request comes in.
Where does your team copy, chase or check the same thing every week?
What would success look like, in your own numbers?

body: You get: where the work gets stuck, and where AI could save you time or money. If the answer doesn’t involve AI, we say so.
From you: someone who knows how the work really gets done, and a real example to walk through.

images.placement: left half of a split; under the lead on mobile
images.alt: A ribbon stream bunching into a knot at a cluster of stones, with one strand slipping through.
images.source: Editorial illustration on a Daylight background, seen from slightly above. A wide satin ribbon in a gradient from Alliance Blue to Ribbon Cyan flows in from the left like a stream across a field of flat faceted paper tiles, then bunches into a loose tangled knot where it meets a cluster of faceted paper stones in the middle of the frame: the place where the work gets stuck, lit clearly so the eye goes straight to it. Beyond the stones a single smooth strand slips through and continues to the right. Soft slate-blue shadows, Partner Navy only in the deepest facets of the stones. Calm empty Daylight space across the top third. Portrait 4:5, safe to crop to 3:4. Palette only: Partner Navy #121B2A, Alliance Blue #1B56FF, Ribbon Cyan #00D5FF, Daylight #F4F7FB and the shades between them. Nature built from satin ribbon and flat paper facets. Light from the upper left, soft navy-tinted shadows falling down and to the right. No text or letters, no people, no hands, no robots, no brains, no circuit boards, no sparkles, no glow, no purple or pink, no regional or cultural motifs, no real places or landmarks.

sections.name: Step 2 · Plan
sections.job: Show that the fix is chosen for the partner, sometimes without AI, and that the plan comes with a fixed quote.
sections.desktop: Navy chapter. Head: title + mono meta (0.9fr) | lead (1.1fr). Two columns: five fix rows with dark service icons and hairlines (620) | Partner 30 sample quote card with [PRICE], label/value rows and a Secondary button. Title set on two balanced lines ('Then we pick / the right fix.') so the accent word never sits alone.
sections.mobile: Title (two balanced lines: 'Then we pick / the right fix.'), meta, lead, five fix rows full width with dark service icons, the sample quote card full width with a full-width Secondary button, then You get / From you.

content.heading: Then we pick the right fix.
content.lead: That might be AI or automation, better design, extra developers or a marketing push. Sometimes it doesn’t involve AI at all.

items.title: AI or automation
items.text: Slow, repetitive work handed to AI and checked by a person.

items.title: Better design
items.text: Apps and websites that are easy to use, designed faster with AI.

items.title: Extra developers
items.text: A developer from our team joins yours, full time, on your tools and your hours.

items.title: A marketing push
items.text: Campaigns, content and ads that bring in more customers.

items.title: No AI at all
items.text: If an off-the-shelf tool or a simpler fix costs you less, we say so.

body: Sample quote card: Your fixed quote, [PRICE]. One price for the whole project, agreed before we start. Includes project management, testing and documentation. Changes are quoted before we do them. No per-seat fees on the tools we build. AI usage passed on at cost, on its own line. You own what we build.
You get: a plan with a fixed quote that lists everything we will charge.
From you: your sign-off on the plan before we build.

sections.name: Step 3 · Build
sections.job: Compare the two ways we build: the whole project for you, or our people inside your team.
sections.desktop: Head with meta, then a 3-column comparison table (row label 240 | We build it for you | We join your team) with service icons in the column heads; You get / From you rows; three service links.
sections.mobile: Table collapses into two stacked cards, one per way of building, each with label/value rows.

content.heading: Two ways to build.
content.lead: Our engineers and designers build what we planned. We take on the whole project, or our people join your team and work inside it.

rows: A defined project, such as a website, an automation or an AI tool
Ongoing work, when you need more hands
Our project lead runs the work and reports to you
You manage our people, backed by all of Alliance AI Partners
In your accounts and tools wherever possible
In your tools, on your hours
A fixed quote before work starts
A person reviews every result before launch
A person reviews every change before it reaches you
You own everything we build, including the code and documentation
You own everything they build for you

body: You get: working software tested with your real data, a short training session and written instructions a new hire can follow.
From you: access to the tools the work needs, and feedback on each weekly update.

sections.name: Step 4 · Run and grow
sections.job: Prove we stay after launch: keep it running, improve it, help the partner grow.
sections.desktop: Full-bleed band 1440x760, image with a navy scrim from the right edge, text block (620) on the right: Display/LG title, mono meta, lead, three hairline rows, note.

content.heading: Then we stay.
content.lead: Where most agencies hand over the project and move on, we keep what we built working, improve it over time and help you win more customers.

items.title: Keep it running
items.text: We watch what we built, fix what breaks and keep AI costs in check.

items.title: Improve it
items.text: Each month we review the numbers with you and agree what to improve next.

items.title: Help you grow
items.text: Marketing and sales work, when you are ready for more customers.

body: You get: a monthly report with the results, AI usage at cost and the plan for next month. Monthly plans you can cancel with [30] days’ notice.

sections.name: Reviewed by a person

content.heading: A person checks every piece of work.
content.lead: Does cheaper mean lower quality? No. AI takes over the repetitive hours, and a person still reviews every piece of work before it reaches you.

items.title: Code
items.text: A person on our team reviews every change before it reaches you.

items.title: Writing
items.text: Articles and landing pages are written faster with AI and checked by people.

items.title: AI agents
items.text: They finish multi-step jobs and check with a person when they are unsure.

items.title: Support replies
items.text: Draft replies wait for your team to approve, and harder cases go to a person.

items.title: Accuracy
items.text: We test AI answers before and after launch, so you can rely on them.

items.title: Documents
items.text: Data pulled from invoices and forms is checked before it is saved.

sections.name: Time zones
sections.job: Show working hours against the partner's day, with sources.
sections.desktop: Asymmetric head; Time zones component (Desktop) with the sample-times note directly under it (a 'Clocks' group, 16 px); three hairline rows (market | what it means | source key); numbered sources.
sections.mobile: Head stacked; Time zones (Mobile, 2x2) with the sample-times note directly under the clocks; three market rows (name + source key, then text); numbered sources.

content.heading: Working hours that fit yours.
content.lead: Project teams work a Manila day, so US partners brief us before they log off and see progress when they log on. Embedded developers work your hours.

items.title: United States
items.text: We work while you sleep. Brief us before you log off, and you will see progress when you log on.

items.title: United Kingdom
items.text: Our afternoon is your morning, so the start of your day overlaps with the end of ours.

items.title: Australia
items.text: Sydney is two hours ahead of us, or three during Australian daylight saving, so most of the working day overlaps.

body: Sample times for a November morning in Manila. The live site shows the real time in each city.

sources.text: NSW Government, Daylight saving (Sydney is UTC+10, or UTC+11 in daylight saving). Retrieved 2026-11-02.
NIST, Local time FAQs (US time zones and daylight saving). Retrieved 2026-11-02.

sections.name: Tools and data
sections.job: Promise that work happens in the partner's tools and their data stays where they decide.
sections.desktop: Asymmetric head; bento: one large card (648) with three icon rows and a link | two stacked cards (ownership; national privacy law with a source key); numbered source.
sections.mobile: Head; large card full width; the two small cards stacked; source.

content.heading: Your data stays in your systems.
content.lead: We work inside the tools you already use. Your data stays where you decide, and we never use it to train anything you don’t own.

items.title: Lessons travel. Your data doesn’t.
items.text: What we learn on one project makes the next one better. Partner data never travels with it.

items.title: You own what we build
items.text: Everything we build is yours, including the code and the documentation.

items.title: A national privacy law
items.text: The Philippines protects personal data under the Data Privacy Act of 2012, enforced by an independent National Privacy Commission.

body: Your data stays in your systems wherever possible.
Everything is written down clearly enough for a new hire to follow.
Every automation has an owner and a backup plan.

sources.text: Republic Act 10173, Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Supreme Court E-Library). Retrieved 2026-11-02.
